author: Linnaeus, 1758
status: 나그네새 수천 마리 · 겨울철새 수백 마리 · 여름에도 드물게 기록(10건 미만)
summary: 봄과 가을에 작은 무리를 지어 규칙적으로 우리나라를 지나가는 나그네새이다. 겨울에는 무리 지어 강가 갈대밭에서 지내고, 여름에는 강가나 호숫가 숲에서 번식하며 물 위로 늘어진 버드나무 가지 끝에 둥지를 매달고 한배에 5~10개, 흔히 7개의 알을 낳는다. 곤충의 유충을 주로 먹고 새끼는 나비목 유충을 먹고 자라며, 겨울에는 풀씨를 먹는다. 한국 일부 지역과 만주, 내몽골, 중국 서북부 윈난 성, 일본 등지에서 번식한다.

points.en: brownish-black forehead, lores, cheeks and ear-coverts
greyish crown with dark shaft streaks
chestnut band on the mantle extending onto the breast

art.subject: Eurasian Penduline Tit (Remiz pendulinus), adult male of the eastern form consobrinus that occurs in Korea, in autumn and winter: forehead, lores, cheeks and ear-coverts form a brownish-black mask; crown and nape greyish with fine dark shaft streaks; a dull white supercilium above the mask; a chestnut band across the upper mantle that spreads onto the sides of the breast; rest of the back, rump and uppertail coverts greyish-buff; wings dark brown with buff and rufous fringes; tail dark brown with pale buff edges; chin white; throat, breast and undertail coverts creamy buff; fine, sharply pointed grey bill with a darker culmen; dark brown eye; dark blue-grey legs.
art.pose: clinging to a reed stem, part of a small flock
art.scene: Korean riverside reedbed in autumn with willows along the bank; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view clinging upright to a reed stem: brownish-black mask from the forehead over the ear-coverts, grey streaked crown, dull white supercilium, chestnut mantle band, greyish-buff back, creamy-buff underparts, needle-fine grey bill, dark blue-grey legs
adult male, front view clinging to a reedmace head: chestnut extending from the mantle onto the breast sides, white chin, creamy-buff throat and breast, dark mask on both sides of the face
art.build: Tiny, compact tit-like bird, clearly smaller than a sparrow, with a rounded body and a fairly short, slightly notched tail. Bill distinctive: short, very fine and sharply pointed, almost needle-like, with a straight culmen, used to pick insects and seeds from reed and reedmace heads. Legs short, dark blue-grey, with strong toes for clinging. Wings short and rounded. Acrobatic: clings sideways or upside-down to reed stems and reedmace heads, usually in small twittering flocks in riverside reedbeds.
avoid: Do not paint a stubby finch-like or tit-like bill; the bill is fine and needle-pointed.
Do not give it a black cap or black bib like a tit (Parus); the crown is grey and the throat white to buff.
Do not give it a long tail like Long-tailed Tit or Vinous-throated Parrotbill.
Do not reduce the mask to a thin eye-line; it is a broad mask covering lores, cheeks and ear-coverts.
